newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-PAKISTAN MAKE BRIGHT START AGAINST ZIMBABWE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN MAKE BRIGHT START AGAINST ZIMBABWE.

text.p: Pakistan, replying to Zimbabwe's first innings 375, lost two quick wickets after a bright start to reach 81 for two at tea on the second day of the first test on Friday.

Left-handers Aamir Sohail and Saeed Anwar raced to 64 in 10.4 overs with Sohail in a particularly aggressive mood, blasting 11 fours in his run-a-ball 46 before falling in the first over by leg spinner Paul Strang.
Pakistan lost their second wicket at 77 when Shadab Kabir, on two, was brilliantly caught in the covers by a diving David Houghton off off-spinner Andrew Whittal.
At tea Anwar was on 30 and Ijaz Ahmad was yet to score.
Zimbabwe, 371 for nine at lunch after starting the day at 240 for six, lasted a further 13 balls after the interval.
Debutant paceman Shahid Nazir rattled the stumps of Henry Olonga to finish with impressive figures of five for 53 while off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq claimed three for 127.
Earlier, Paul Strang, 37 overnight, went on to make an unbeaten 106 for his maiden test century while opener Grant Flower hit 110.
Opener Flower, 98 overnight, completed the second test hundred of his career by driving paceman Shahid Nazir for his 12th four.
He eventually fell to off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq having added a Zimbabwe record 131 runs for the seventh wicket with Strang.
Strang, not out 37 at the start of the day, reached his maiden test century by taking two runs off Wasim Akram after the Pakistani captain had taken the second new ball in the 103rd over.
Strang, playing his 10th test, was twice dropped by Shadab Kabir off Waqar Younis on his way to his century, which he reached in 301 minutes with the help of nine fours.
He put on 87 runs with his brother Bryan (42), erasing Zimbabwe's previous best ninth-wicket partnership of 40.
